chapters.name: Food industries/animal fodder
chapters.citation: Profundo (Feb 2025), 'EUDR Compliance Costs: Economic analysis'. Average cost 0.10% of revenue across 12 forest-risk commodity firms; upper bound 0.32%; SME 0.17%. Soy is on EUDR Annex I list. Conservative 1.0%. https://farmforce.com/articles/the-real-cost-of-eudr-compliance-what-agri-commodities-companies-need-to-know/

chapters.name: Oil seeds/oleaginous fruits
chapters.citation: Profundo (Feb 2025). Soy is EUDR-listed (Reg 2023/1115 Annex I). Same compliance-cost methodology as HS 23. https://farmforce.com/articles/the-real-cost-of-eudr-compliance-what-agri-commodities-companies-need-to-know/

chapters.name: Coffee, tea, mate and spices
chapters.citation: Profundo (Feb 2025): coffee specifically estimated at 0.018% consumer-price impact, ~0.10% of company revenue. Coffee is EUDR-listed. https://news.mongabay.com/2025/03/eudr-compliance-costs-to-be-minimal-report-finds-but-industry-disagrees/

chapters.name: Ores, slag and ash
chapters.citation: Not EUDR-listed, not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Pulp of wood
chapters.citation: Profundo (Feb 2025). Wood/pulp is EUDR-listed; replaces EUTR which had ~0.1-0.3% compliance overhead.

chapters.name: Mineral fuels
chapters.citation: CBAM includes hydrogen and electricity in primary scope. Refined fuel products (HS 27) adjacent but not in current scope. Conservative 0.5%. https://www.iisd.org/articles/explainer/eu-carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism-bigger-trade-implications

chapters.name: Tobacco
chapters.citation: Not on EUDR Annex I, not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Fruit and nuts
chapters.citation: EC (2014) farmer compliance study: differential vs third countries averages well under 1%; conservative 1% applied to fruit for pesticide-residue standards gap. https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2019-12/ext-study-farmer-costs-exec_sum_2014_en_0.pdf

chapters.name: Pharmaceutical products
chapters.citation: Not in CBAM scope, no relevant agri-environmental wedge.

chapters.name: Prep. vegetables/fruits/olives
chapters.citation: EC (2014) farmer compliance study, food-safety / pesticide-residue standards differential. Applied conservatively at 1.0%. https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2019-12/ext-study-farmer-costs-exec_sum_2014_en_0.pdf

chapters.name: Chemical products n.e.c.
chapters.citation: CBAM covers fertilizers in primary scope. HS 38 (chemicals n.e.c.) is mixed; only fertilizer subset directly covered. Estimated weighted ad valorem 2.0%. https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en

chapters.name: Machinery/boilers/reactors
chapters.citation: Currently outside CBAM scope. Proposed 2034 downstream extension (auto sector) gave 4.6% for Chinese exports; for current EU-Mercosur machinery the sourced value is essentially zero today.

chapters.name: Plastics and articles thereof
chapters.citation: Not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Aluminium and articles
chapters.citation: Aluminium is in CBAM primary scope. Frontier Economics + IISD: 2.6-4.6% ad valorem equivalent for downstream goods; primary aluminium imports central 3.0%. https://www.iisd.org/articles/explainer/eu-carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism-bigger-trade-implications

chapters.name: Electrical machinery
chapters.citation: Not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Aircraft/spacecraft
chapters.citation: Not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Tools/cutlery
chapters.citation: Steel content present but not CBAM declarant.

chapters.name: Iron/steel articles
chapters.citation: Iron and steel is in CBAM primary scope. Frontier Economics + IISD estimate 2.6-4.6% ad valorem for downstream automotive; direct steel imports likely higher; central 3.0%. https://www.iisd.org/articles/explainer/eu-carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism-bigger-trade-implications

chapters.name: Commodities n.e.c.
chapters.citation: Residual category, no relevant wedge.

chapters.name: Stone/cement articles
chapters.citation: Cement is in CBAM primary scope. Articles (HS 68) carry the embedded cement CBAM cost. Central 3.0%. https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en

chapters.name: Salt/stone/cement
chapters.citation: Mixed category. Cement directly CBAM-listed; salt and stone not. Weighted estimate 2.0%.

chapters.name: Ships/boats
chapters.citation: Not CBAM-listed.

chapters.name: Beverages/wine
chapters.citation: Wine is NOT on EUDR Annex I (EUDR covers cattle, wood, soy, palm oil, rubber, coffee, cocoa). Wine is NOT in CBAM primary scope. The energy-intensity argument used in v3 was not a sourced quantitative basis. Revised to zero in v4.

chapters.name: Dairy produce; birds' eggs; natural honey
chapters.citation: European Commission (2014), 'Assessing farmers' costs of compliance with EU legislation in environment, animal welfare and food safety'. 1.0% wedge captures compliance differential. Dairy is not directly EUDR-listed. EU MFN ~45% phases over 6 years; Feta has separate 7-year GI transition. Mercosur 28% phases over 10 years. https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2019-12/ext-study-farmer-costs-exec_sum_2014_en_0.pdf

chapters.name: Animal or vegetable fats and oils
chapters.citation: European Commission (2014) farmer compliance study. Olive oil has 25% F2F yield-loss exposure (Wageningen) but the wedge captures bilateral compliance asymmetry, not yield. 1.0%. EU MFN ~8% phases over 10 years; Mercosur ~16% phases over 6 years. https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2019-12/ext-study-farmer-costs-exec_sum_2014_en_0.pdf

22.reason: TRQ only covers ethanol; HS 22 is mostly wine/spirits at bilateral level
